findings.measured: The audio is still loud at the last sample; the ending may be cut off.

steps.text: Extend the timeline selection past the last reverb and delay tails, then File › Bounce Mix again.

other_options.text: Select the end of the last clip, press Command-F to add a fade-out, and bounce again.

notes.headline: This mix is in good shape for mastering — the only real issue is that the file stops while audio is still playing.
notes.summary: Your levels, headroom and stereo picture all measure well for a mix going to mastering: -14.38 LUFS integrated with -1.27 dBTP true peak leaves plenty of room for a mastering engineer to work. The one thing to fix is the ending — the audio is still loud at the last sample, so the tail is likely chopped. Re-bounce with the selection extended past the tails and you're at a 10.0.

priorities.title: The bounce cuts off while audio is still playing
priorities.why: A hard cut at the last sample reads as a click or an abrupt stop, and mastering can't restore a tail that was never captured. It also makes fades and song transitions on the release harder to judge.

listen_for: Play the last few seconds of the new bounce and confirm the reverb and delay tails decay fully into silence rather than stopping.
Listen to the very end on headphones at raised volume — any remaining click or truncation will be obvious there.
strengths: True peak of -1.27 dBTP and peak-to-loudness of 13.1 dB leave healthy headroom and dynamics for mastering.
Stereo image is solid: 0.785 L/R correlation, 0.793 in the low end, and only 0.5 dB mono loss.
Left/right balance is essentially centered at 0.02 dB.
